title: Sprint Germination Lab: seed-to-rollout sketch
body:
Context / hypothesis:
- We keep losing 1-2 days per small experiment because the path from idea -> rollout requires juggling SDK flags, infra requests, and ad-hoc cost estimates.
- Hypothesis: a lightweight 'germination' flow (seed -> sprout -> rollout) that packages a quick config + estimate + canary scaffold will reduce friction and increase safe experiment velocity.

What is a "germination" flow (very rough):
- Seed: author a tiny experiment descriptor (name, user cohort, target QPS, target latency SLO, qualitative goal) -> system returns quick cost delta and a suggested config (batching, quantization hint, QoS tier).
- Sprout: one-click create of a canary route with suggested model variant(s), auto-generated telemetry hooks, and short TTL.
- Rollout: guided checklist to convert a sprout into an actual route (pin model, add alerts, SLA billing opt-in).

Why this is different:
- Not a full PRD for route editor; focused on speed and guardrails for small experiments, with cost-aware defaults from Optimize.
- Hybrid UX: CLI quickseed + Console guided sprout -> infra-friendly YAML for teams that want to check-in to GitHub.

User stories (ranked):
1) As an engineer prototyping a new prompt variant, I want a 2-minute flow to launch a canary at 5 QPS and get an upfront cost delta and expected p50/p95 latency, so I can validate assumptions without infra tickets.
2) As a product manager, I want to attach a short objective and success metric to each germination so experiments are discoverable in the experiments board.
3) As an SRE, I need automatic alert scaffolding and a kill-switch toggle on every sprout so experiments don't cause incidents.
4) As a billing analyst, I want the germination flow to estimate monthly run rate extrapolated from the canary so we can flag potential budget overruns.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- [ ] CLI: `rw germinate create --name "quick-nlu-variant" --qps 5 --target p95=300ms --budget-estimate` returns a suggested config and cost delta within 10 seconds.
- [ ] Console: "Germinate" quicktile that seeds a sprout with one-click canary creation; sprout has a 24h TTL default.
- [ ] Generated canary route includes: telemetry hooks, basic alerts (error rate, p95 > target), and a kill-switch.
- [ ] Cost estimate surfaced in UI and CLI referencing Optimize heuristics; show top-3 levers affecting cost (batching, quantization, seq-length).
- [ ] Experiment metadata stored and visible on experiments board (owner, goal, start/stop times).

Metrics to track success:
- Time from idea -> canary created (target: < 10 minutes for CLI, < 3 minutes for Console).
- Number of germinations/month and percent that convert into rollouts.
- Incidents caused by germinated canaries (target: zero high-sev).
- Accuracy of cost estimates vs observed (target: within 20% for first 24h).

Rough UX flow (notes to self):
- CLI first: fast path for engineers. Example: `rw germinate seed --name=reply-tweak --qps=8 --goal="reduce hallucination for receipts"` -> returns config YAML and `rw germinate sprout --from=last-seed`.
- Console: small modal on the Routes page: "Germinate a canary" with 4 fields and an expandable advanced pane. Show cost delta live as fields change.
- Sprout page: countdown TTL, button to "Pin and Rollout" with checklist, link to create GH PR for config.

API/infra notes (very preliminary):
- New lightweight artifact: germination manifest (YAML) with: name, owner, qps, latency_slo, budget_hint, suggested_model_variants, telemetry_profile, ttl_hours.
- Runtime: sprout routes should be scheduled on a lower-priority pool by default (to reduce blast radius).
- Billing: sprout usage should be tagged immediately so billing signals can be captured and filtered.

Engineering effort (guesstimate):
- CLI plumbing + backend seed endpoint: 2-3 dev weeks.
- Console UI + short TTL lifecycle + experiments board integration: 3-4 dev weeks (product + FE).
- Telemetry scaffolding + alerts + kill-switch: 1-2 weeks SRE collaboration.
- Cost estimator integration with Optimize heuristics: 1-2 weeks (may be iterative).

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: inaccurate cost estimates could lead to bad decisions. Mitigation: conservative default multiplier and explicit confidence band.
- Risk: too many sprout routes consume capacity. Mitigation: enforce soft limits per-user/org and default lower-priority placement.
- Risk: experiments become persistent (TTL bypassed). Mitigation: audit job to flag sprouts older than TTL and auto-suspend unless pinned.

Open questions (needs product/research):
- Should germination manifests be first-class Git objects / stored in repo by default? Pros: traceability. Cons: slows the fast path.
- What default model variants do we recommend? Small, medium, large? Or choose by latency SLO?
- How to show cost estimate when model is multi-variant fallback chain? Do we show worst-case or expected-case?

Parking lot (ideas if this lands):
- Seed templates for common goals (NLG quality tuning, latency bench, embedding index experiments).
- Automated experiment summary: after TTL ends, generate a short auto-report (usage, cost, key metrics) and suggest next steps.
- Shared library of germination manifests for company teams to clone.

Immediate next steps (for next 1-2 weeks):
- Sync with Rowan and Marta to decide CLI surface (short meeting).
- Draft lightweight germination manifest proto and post to #product-germination for feedback.
- Prototype Console tile mock in Figma (I can sketch low-fidelity today).

To-dos (personal):
- [ ] Write seed manifest example (YAML) and include in PRD sketch.
- [ ] Add a simple cost formula stub that references Optimize heuristics.
- [ ] Schedule 30m with Rowan, Marta, Ishaan (invite tentative attendees).

Random notes / rough YAML sketch: 
---
name: quick-nlu-reply-test
owner: zoya.rahman@redwood.ai
qps: 5
latency_slo_ms: 350
budget_hint_currency_per_month: "$15"
suggested_models: ["rw-medium-q2", "rw-small-q2"]
telemetry_profile: "experiment-basic"
ttl_hours: 24
---

Footer: this doc is a scratchpad — full PRD would include compliance review for any public customer experiments and a small playbook for product managers.

Notes-to-self: avoid overengineering the first iteration; fast wins = CLI seed + console sprout tile + tag-based billing.
